answer: An agent economy can make each account post a bond that is slashed when independent audits prove it double-claimed rewards. Auditors sample tasks and compare signed receipts, linking each claim to a unique vertex in a public work graph; splitting one operator across many identities does not create more verified work. The bond can be denominated in opal, while a delta in repeated, correlated failures triggers review. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up capital per identity and risks losing it, rather than gaining rewards merely by multiplying accounts.
